About Bolna

That’s this role. You’ll listen to real calls, annotate what actually happened, and check whether our automated systems - LLM-as-judge evals and quantitative signal detection - got it right. What You’ll Do

Annotation

  • Listen to and annotate real customer calls - transcription review, issue tagging, labeling - using tools like Label Studio

  • Follow (and help sharpen) annotation guidelines for a multilingual environment (Hindi, English, Hinglish, )

Verifying LLM-as-Judge Evaluations

  • For calls flagged by our automated eval pipeline, verify whether the model’s call was actually correct - for example, confirming whether a detected barge-in (agent/customer talking over each other) genuinely happened by listening to the audio

  • Mark agreements and disagreements clearly, with reasoning, so we can measure and improve model accuracy over time

  • All tools needed for this will be provided

Verifying Quantitative Measures

  • Check system-flagged quantitative signals against the actual call - e.g., confirming whether an “agent interruption” the system detected really occurred at that timestamp

  • Flag false positives/negatives so we can tighten detection logic

  • Help identify edge cases that current rubrics or detection logic don’t handle well


Inspecting Calls & Surfacing New Issues

  • Bring these patterns back to the team so rubrics, prompts, and detection logic keep improving

jobs.description:
Software Engineer – Systems & Reliability

Smallest.ai | Bangalore

About The Role

Own a service or a part of our product from design through production. You’ll write the code, validate its behaviour, deploy it and keep it reliable for the customers who depend on it.

Testing, deployment and operations are part of engineering ownership here. You’ll work with the team, but you won’t hand off responsibility when your code is merged.

Our systems power real-time voice, where an extra 100 milliseconds can change how a conversation feels. Behind that experience are GPU inference workloads for text-to-speech and speech recognition across AWS regions, alongside multi-tenant APIs, concurrency controls, billing and webhooks.

We work with Python, TypeScript and Go on Kubernetes in AWS, supported by Redis, MongoDB-compatible stores, Postgres, ClickHouse, RabbitMQ and Temporal. Familiarity helps; understanding the mechanisms underneath matters more.

What you’ll own

  • Define success before building. Establish measurable service-level objectives for customer-facing latency, availability and correctness.

  • Write maintainable code. Build systems another engineer can understand, debug and operate without depending on you being available.

  • Test beyond the happy path. Use unit, integration, load and fault-injection testing to validate behaviour under realistic conditions. Explain your coverage and its limitations in review.

  • Ship safely. Own CI, deployments, rollbacks, schema migrations and infrastructure changes. When your work requires a Terraform change, you own that too.

  • Operate what you build. Create useful dashboards, actionable alerts and runbooks. Participate in on-call, incident response and postmortems.

  • Stay close to customer impact. When calls drop or requests fail, investigate directly, communicate clearly and drive the issue to resolution.

  • Improve the system around the problem. Turn recurring incidents and manual debugging into better controls, automation and tooling.



The challenges you’ll help solve

Our product works, and we’re strengthening the reliability practices that support its next stage of growth.

  • Define SLOs for services that do not yet have clear reliability targets.

  • Replace misleading health signals with monitoring that reflects whether customers can complete their tasks.

  • Improve logging, health checks and alerting so failures are easier to detect and diagnose.

  • Make testing and operational readiness a consistent part of delivery.

  • Address existing reliability gaps alongside new product development.

You’ll fix problems you didn’t introduce and make decisions with incomplete information. You’ll also be expected to balance delivery speed with production readiness: surface risks early, propose practical trade-offs and follow through on commitments.

What we look for

Strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to apply them to unfamiliar problems. We assess these directly through technical discussion and practical reasoning.

You should be comfortable explaining and reasoning about:

  • Processes and operating systems: Process creation, signals, file descriptors, namespaces, cgroups, PID 1 behaviour and CPU throttling.

  • Memory: Virtual memory, page cache, available memory, swap, cgroup memory limits, out-of-memory behaviour and stalls that occur despite low CPU utilisation.

  • Files and storage: Inodes, durability and fsync, disk-usage discrepancies, atomic rename, IOPS and throughput.

  • Networking: TCP states, TIME_WAIT, connection and read timeouts, Nagle’s algorithm, delayed acknowledgements, DNS, TLS, NAT and the trade-offs of UDP for real-time media.

  • Concurrency and distributed systems: Race conditions, locks, idempotency, at-least-once delivery, retries, backoff, jitter, backpressure, clocks and partial failures.

  • Language runtimes: Event loops, blocking operations, garbage collection, the Python GIL, memory leaks and algorithmic costs at production scale.

  • Data systems: Indexes, query plans, transaction isolation, row and column stores, and replication lag.

  • Reliability: SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, latency percentiles, why percentiles cannot simply be averaged, and alerting on customer-visible symptoms.

We also value clear writing, the patience to read unfamiliar code and the habit of measuring before drawing conclusions.

We evaluate demonstrated ability rather than years of experience, previous titles, employers, degrees, colleges, certifications or the number of frameworks on your résumé.

How we work

  • Be honest about what you know. “I don’t know” is useful when followed by a clear approach to finding out.

  • Share hypotheses early. Make your reasoning visible, invite scrutiny and update your view when the evidence changes.

  • Take responsibility and improve the mechanism. Our postmortems focus on contributing causes and concrete changes that prevent recurrence.

  • Start with the customer’s experience. A healthy pod does not mean a successful call. If the caller hears silence, we investigate it as a failure.

  • Use evidence. Reach for traces, packet captures, profilers, query plans and load tests to understand what is happening.

  • Challenge ideas respectfully. Question decisions—including those made by founders—with clear reasoning and evidence.

  • Automate repeated work. When a problem keeps returning, build a better way to detect, diagnose or resolve it.

  • Move with urgency. Make decisions at the right level, act on reversible steps and communicate blockers early. Use meetings when they help resolve a decision.

  • Hold yourself to the standard you expect from others. Give direct, constructive feedback and receive it with the same openness.

What to expect

This is a hands-on role with substantial accountability. It includes on-call responsibilities, occasional incidents outside regular hours, customer escalations and debugging across systems you may not have built.

You’ll do well here if you enjoy understanding how systems work, acting quickly and staying with a problem until it is resolved.

This role may not suit you if you prefer narrowly defined implementation tasks, consider your responsibility complete at merge, or expect testing and production operations to sit entirely with another team.

Why join Smallest.ai

Build systems where engineering decisions are audible in the customer experience. You’ll work across real-time voice, GPU inference and distributed infrastructure, with the opportunity to improve both the product and how we build and operate it.

Your impact will show up in faster responses, fewer failed calls, safer releases and systems the whole team can trust.

jobs.title: Finance and Accounting Specialist (SaaS/US Clients) | June 2026 Start
jobs.description:
About the Role

You're the person merchants call when their numbers don't add up. When a Shopify payout doesn't reconcile with the P&L, when COGS looks off, when a multi-currency gap shows up, you dig in, find the root cause, and walk the merchant through it. These are high-growth eCommerce brands selling across Shopify, Amazon, Walmart, and TikTok Shop. They use Fulfil as their ERP, and you're their first point of contact when something doesn't tie out.

You'll work with merchants ranging from D2C founders doing their own books to finance teams at 9-figure brands, both of whom need you to be sharp, clear, and confident on the call. Internally, you'll partner with our Engineering, Implementation, and Success teams in Bangalore.

If you thrive on variety, own problems end-to-end, and can explain a multi-currency FX discrepancy to a non-accountant in under two minutes, keep reading.

About Fulfil

Fulfil is an ERP built for high-growth eCommerce brands. Our merchants run complex, multi-channel operations across Shopify, Amazon, Walmart, TikTok Shop, and beyond relying on Fulfil to keep their financials accurate, reconciled, and audit-ready.

What You'll Actually Do

Day-to-day, you will:

  • Own merchant accounting issues end-to-end: troubleshoot reconciliation discrepancies between Fulfil and sales channels like Shopify and Amazon, and walk merchants through exactly what went wrong and why

  • Guide merchants on eCommerce accounting fundamentals: support merchants with COGS tracking, inventory valuation, revenue recognition, and multi-channel transaction reconciliation within Fulfil

  • Implementation support: partner with the Implementation team on new merchant onboarding and advising on accounting workflow design, chart of accounts setup, and core financial configuration to ensure merchants go live on solid footing 

  • Communicate clearly to diverse audiences: explain financial concepts to both technically savvy controllers and accountant-averse founders

  • Support merchants through audits: help them pull the right documentation and reconciliations from Fulfil

  • Advise on compliance and currency exposure: help merchants navigate sales tax across geographies (multiple US states, Canadian provinces, UK and others) and multi-currency accounting considerations

  • Lead product adoption: identify where merchants are underutilizing Fulfil’s financial features, run targeted training session and consult on process improvements to drive longer-term value 

  • Collaborate cross-functionally: surface recurring merchant pain points to Implementation, Support, and Engineering teams to shape product enhancements

  • Leverage AI to move faster: use tools like Claude to clarify accounting treatments, compress context, or draft merchant updates

A realistic day might look like:

  • Helping come up with a cutover plan for a merchant migrating from their current accounting software to Fulfil

  • Helping a user troubleshoot and reconcile discrepancies within their ledger balances

  • Conducting a training session with users, consulting and providing best practices

  • Working closely with our product team by iterating on customer feedback

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years of accounting, audit, or finance-SaaS implementation/support experience — at an eCommerce company, a multi-client accounting BPO with eCommerce clients, a US/UK-focused accounting BPO, or as a functional/implementation consultant on a finance ERP 

  • Hands-on working experience reconciling and closing books, not just familiarity

  • Strong understanding of US GAAP and eCommerce-specific accounting: revenue recognition across channels, COGS, inventory valuation, and settlement reconciliation

  • Excellent customer-facing communication skills for daily live calls and async communication with North American merchants, including C-suite stakeholders

  • Comfort with ambiguity, context-switching, and ownership without waiting to be told what to do next

Nice to have

  • Experience at a US-focused accounting firm or eCommerce aggregator

  • Working knowledge of US multi-state sales tax compliance and multi-currency accounting

  • CA, CPA, or ACCA designation paired with demonstrated client-facing or advisory experience

  • Hands-on experience with NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QBO, Xero, Zoho Books, or Tally

Fair Warning

  • This role is not for someone looking for a traditional internal accounting or bookkeeping seat. Closing books is table stakes here, not the job, the job is sitting across from merchants and untangling their numbers with them.

  • It's not for someone who'd rather work behind a spreadsheet than on a Zoom call. You'll be live with North American merchants daily, founders, controllers, C-suite, explaining their numbers in plain language.

  • It's not for someone who needs the next step laid out for them. Tickets land messy, context shifts, and we figure it out in motion. The right person finds that fun.

  • And if AI is something you've been meaning to get around to, we're not the place to figure it out. You should be using Claude or similar tools in your workflow already.

Everyone Ships Every Day

We're building the ERP that fast-growing eCommerce brands actually want to use, which means we're taking on entrenched enterprise software with a small, intense team.

Big Tech and VC-backed startups are 400-horsepower engines running at 25% efficiency — bloated teams, endless meetings, six months to ship a feature. At Fulfil, we're a 200-horsepower engine running at 100%. We're bootstrapped, profitable, and growing steadily. No permission layers. No "alignment meetings" about alignment meetings. Everyone ships every day.

The work: You'll own meaningful problems with direct customer impact. Our customers run 24/7 operations across time zones, and when they're launching on BFCM or scaling from $10M to $100M, they need us to move fast. That urgency flows downstream. This is high-intensity work with real consequences.

What high-intensity actually means:

  • Most weeks are 45-55 hours; peak seasons (BFCM, major launches) hit 60+

  • Occasional off-hours calls with our distributed team or for customer launches

  • Long days (10+ hours) aren't uncommon

  • The work doesn't pause even if we try to protect your focus time

What you get in return:

  • Real autonomy over execution (we measure impact, not facetime)

  • Ownership of problems that matter to real businesses

  • Unlimited PTO, we actually want you to use (we'd rather you rest than burn out)

You'll thrive here if you get energy from building something that matters, want ownership over outcomes vs tasks, are open to direct feedback in public Slack channels, and like moving fast without red tape.

This isn't for you if you need a strict 40-hour boundary, prefer structured oversight, or want work to be a contained part of your life.
